title: Find Mismatched Segments Between Two Strings
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<vector<string>> res: this is the returned output, not counted
- local ints i, start, n: O(1)
- substrings stored only inside the returned vector, not counted
- no recursion, no auxiliary containers
approach: Scan both strings left to right with a single index. Whenever s1[i] != s2[i], mark the start and keep advancing while the characters still differ; when they match again (or the strings end), emit [s1.substr(start, len), s2.substr(start, len)]. Equal characters act as hard boundaries that no mismatched segment can cross, so one linear pass captures every maximal run.
hints: When s1[i] and s2[i] are equal at some index, can a single mismatched segment ever include that index? The constraints say both strings have the same length, so every position is comparable one-to-one.

Use a single linear scan with a start marker. In Example 1 ("earth" vs "empty"), index 1 differs ('a' vs 'm'), so mark start=1 and extend through index 2; index 3 matches ('t'=='t'), so close the segment and emit s1[1..2]="ar" and s2[1..2]="mp".

**Single character mismatch** - n=1, the only position differs
`Input: s1 = "a", s2 = "b"` → `Expected: [["a","b"]]`
⚠️ Bug: using `while i < n-1` in the inner loop → returns `[]`

**Single character match** - n=1, the only position is equal
`Input: s1 = "a", s2 = "a"` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: pushing a segment on every iteration without checking the mismatch condition → returns `[["a","a"]]`

**All characters differ** - the whole string is one segment
`Input: s1 = "abc", s2 = "xyz"` → `Expected: [["abc","xyz"]]`
⚠️ Bug: stopping the inner extension at `i < n-1` instead of `i < n` → returns `[["ab","xy"]]`

**Mismatch only at the last index** - segment touches the right boundary
`Input: s1 = "aat", s2 = "aaz"` → `Expected: [["t","z"]]`
⚠️ Bug: checking `i+1 < n` before extending, so the final index is never reached → returns `[]`

**All equal** - no segments at all
`Input: s1 = "aaa", s2 = "aaa"` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: always pushing at least one (possibly empty) segment at the end → returns `[["",""]]`

followUps.q: The strings are up to 10^9 characters long and arrive as two streams you can read once; how do you adapt?
followUps.a: Keep a running buffer for the current mismatched segment only, flushing [sub1, sub2] whenever a match is seen or the stream ends. Time stays O(n) and auxiliary memory drops to O(L) where L is the longest segment, since you never hold the whole strings.

followUps.q: Return only mismatched segments whose length is at least k; what changes?
followUps.a: Add `if (i - start >= k)` before pushing into the result. The scan is unchanged, so time remains O(n) and auxiliary space O(1).

followUps.q: The strings may have different lengths because of insertions/deletions; find aligned mismatched blocks.
followUps.a: This becomes an edit-script / diff problem: compute the LCS or run Myers' diff to get matching anchors, then group the gaps between anchors into mismatched blocks. Time rises to O(n*m) for classic LCS or O((n+m)*d) for Myers where d is the edit distance.
